scheduleClassification.settledSuccess: A pass-through observer on the exact original PhiTransfer.download Promise aborts the caller at fulfillment, yields one microtask for the original consumer finally, then re-enters. The original producer is already fulfilled and cannot be retroactively rejected. This is programmatic/API settlement robustness, NOT a reproduction from an ordinary physical click. No synthetic success value or engine is used.
scheduleClassification.pendingFailure: First actual native response is held after clone validation. Caller cancellation and replacement finish before the old response is delivered; the original transfer then produces its own AbortError. Only delivery order is controlled.
scheduleClassification.releaseBudget: Node reproduction uses original PhiTransfer with simultaneous complete Response bodies and no producer observer. Browser first obtains and hashes native original bodies, buffers each into one Response chunk, and releases all three together. This aligns completion deliberately; unmodified native-body scheduling did not reproduce the capacity defect in the initial browser run.
scheduleClassification.quality: Node controlled clock and real transfer functions, synthetic byte input; not live bandwidth or a physical network-incidence measurement.
